podcast.body: The "surrealist" lead single from Nirvana's "In Utero," this song topped the modern rock chart by October 1993, reinforcing the band's continued chart dominance. "It's lead single, The Surrealist Heart-shaped Box, topped the modern rock chart by October."

podcast.body: The CD single version of "Heart-Shaped Box" included "Mera Gold" as its final track. This was significant as "Mera Gold" is the only song in the entire Nirvana canon not written or sung by Kurt Cobain, having originated from Dave Grohl's solo work and being recorded during the *In Utero* sessions. Its placement on the single meant it was "buried" but still released. "It is the only song in the whole Nirvana canon, not written or sung by Kurt Cobain."

podcast.body: This song is cited as an example of grunge music utilizing a drop D tuning. This tuning was inspired by the guitar sound of Tony Iommi's Black Sabbath, which itself originated from an industrial accident involving sheet metal. "Nirvana's heart shape box recorded using a drop D tuning inspired by the sound of Tony Iome's Black Sabbath guitar, which was directly caused by an industrial accident involving sheet metal."
